reconcile.connective: Commentators read "cut off" and "put to death" as one judicial sentence — or as two coordinated sanctions — so a single penalty stands behind the differing wording.

discrepancy.connective: Jacob Milgrom presses the lever the objection turns on, holding that karet ("cut off") is a distinct divine penalty — extirpation by God's own hand — categorically separate from the human death sentence, so the two formulations name two different sanctions.

skeptic.name: Jacob Milgrom
skeptic.attribution: Jacob Milgrom (d. 2010), Numbers (JPS Torah Commentary, 1990); cf. Leviticus 1-16 (Anchor Bible 3, 1991)

excerpts.excerpt_text: that soul shall be cut off from among his people; that is, shall die by the hand of the civil magistrate, it being but another phrase for being put to death;
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly equates 'cut off' with 'put to death' as one and the same penalty, dissolving the karet-vs-execution tension. Central on-tension note.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Shall surely be put to death - The magistrates shall examine into the business, and if the accused be found guilty, he shall be stoned to death. … Shall be cut off - Because that person who could so far contemn the Sabbath, which was a sign to them of the rest which remained for the people of God, was of course an infidel, and should be cut off from all the privileges and expectations of an Israelite.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Reads the two clauses as two coordinated sanctions on one offender (civil execution plus excommunicatory cutting-off), harmonizing them as compatible rather than rival penalties.

excerpts.excerpt_text: It is true that it had already been laid down in Exo 31:14-15, and Exo 35:2, that any breach of the law of the Sabbath should be punished by death and extermination, but the mode had not yet been prescribed.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Harmonizes the Numbers 15 narrative with the Exodus statutes: the death-and-extermination penalty was fixed; only the manner (stoning) was newly disclosed, so the texts agree on the sanction.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Exodus 31:14
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, arguing 'cut off' is 'but another phrase for being put to death,' and elsewhere notes the Jarchi distinction (magistrate vs. the hand of God) for the secret offender.
